name: Iran
research_note: Only 2 of the planned ~9 searches ran before the session-wide WebSearch budget (200/200) was exhausted. Everything below is from those 2 result sets. Statements marked 'background' are the researcher's prior knowledge, not a snippet, and should be re-verified.

nso.name: Statistical Centre of Iran (Markaz-e Amar-e Iran)
nso.note: The office's own site did not surface in either search; what surfaced were a provincial portal (Tehran province, amar.thmporg.ir), the GHDx catalogue entry for the 2016 census, the open-data mirror Iran Open Data (iranopendata.org) and a commercial mirror (iranstatis.com). The URL is left null rather than typed from memory.

latest_census.notes: General Census of Population and Housing 1395, conducted 25 Mehr to 25 Aban 1395 (Oct-Nov 2016); 79,926,270 people (fa.wikipedia snippet). Religion IS asked, in the state's recognised categories (Muslim, Christian, Zoroastrian, Jewish, other/not stated -- background). Secondary sources quote it: over 99% Muslim; 117,700 Christians of recognised denominations; 23,109 Zoroastrians (2023 US IRF report and ARDA); and 'According to the 2016 Census, Khuzestan Province was home to sixty-eight Jews' -- a PROVINCE-level census figure, which is the evidence that religion was published subnationally. Ethnicity and mother tongue have never been Iranian census questions (background; consistent with the packet's free-text ethnicity record and with MRG relying on estimates). Whether a 1405 (2025/26) round has been run or published was not researched.

tier_reason: Religion is a census question and a province-level 2016 census figure is quoted by a secondary source, so a count by 31 ostans (= admin1) exists; but the SCI table itself (URL, format) was not located, so it is 'exists but costly' until someone finds it. Ethnicity and language are not asked and should be declared not_collected.
recommended_action: Search the SCI site and iranopendata.org for the 1395 census 'jam'iyat bar hasb-e din' (population by religion) table by ostan; expect a spreadsheet, and expect the non-Muslim categories to be tiny (Christians 117,700 nationally). Reconcile the packet's 32 admin1 shapes with Iran's 31 provinces before joining. Declare ethnicity and language not_collected with the reason 'no Iranian census has asked ethnicity or mother tongue' once a snippet confirms it (the packet's free-text ethnicity record is the same absence). Nothing was found or searched for the 431 shahrestans (admin2); SCI's per-province detailed volumes may carry religion by shahrestan -- check one province's volume before assuming. IPUMS-International holds Iranian census samples (background) but was not searched.

summary: Iran's 2016 (1395) census asks religion in the state's recognised categories and the figures were published by province -- the 2023 IRF report quotes the census for 68 Jews in Khuzestan -- so a 31-ostan count exists that would join to admin1 (the packet draws 32 shapes; reconcile first). The Statistical Centre of Iran's own table was not located in the two searches that ran, and its site did not surface at all; the Tehran-province portal and Iran Open Data show SCI provincial tables are republished online. Ethnicity and mother tongue are not census questions and should be declared not_collected. Tier B: find the SCI or iranopendata.org religion-by-ostan spreadsheet, then check one province's detailed volume for a shahrestan cut before assuming admin2 is empty.
